waste_markers.label: Words of docs
waste_markers.note: about 12 novels; 49% of commits were docs-only

waste_markers.label: PHP lines that are comments or blank
Decision IDs, names and dates in product code

featured_note: SPEC §7 asks for 3 keep, 3 change, 2 drop on the bakery page. 'featured' marks a suggested set; the copy lane may swap.

keep.title: A fresh reviewer, a 9/10 pass mark and a cap on rounds
keep.detail: Every failed round found a real bug.

keep.title: Staging first, my phone check, my "passed", my push
keep.detail: My staging check caught a pricing bug that review had passed.

keep.title: One decision at a time, with a recommended answer
Two lanes by risk (small vs feature)
keep.detail: Nine small-lane features later passed scored review anyway.

keep.title: Record and ask for bugs outside the task
A few hard rules, each checked by a machine
keep.detail: The plugin works with the theme off.

keep.title: Machinery deferred until needed
keep.detail: The token engine was never needed.

keep.title: A fresh session from a short written brief when the context got heavy
One name per source of truth
I close the review threads, never the AI

change.title: Ticket prompts of 3,000–7,000 words
change.detail: Builders needed a continuation per ticket.
change.instead: Size tickets to fit one session; keep briefs to one page.

change.title: Tests that pinned file fingerprints, literal markup and exact text
change.detail: They broke on every unrelated change (161 re-pins).
change.instead: Test behaviour; check looks by eye.

change.title: One shared local database for all parallel sessions
change.detail: It meant a lock, announcements, a database recovery and test orders leaking into Mailchimp.
change.instead: Each lane gets its own data.

change.title: STATUS as the single source of truth grew to 99k words
The decision register
change.detail: 694 of 1,529 rows never got signed off.
change.instead: Log only behaviour-changing decisions, 1–2 lines each, signed off in batches.

change.title: Many Terminal workers
change.detail: They worked but were fragile: invisible workers, dead windows, a stalled worker, SSH dropping overnight.
change.instead: Use 2–3 lanes at most and check each one is alive.

change.title: Memory used as a state log
change.detail: Ticket snapshots duplicated STATUS, and the index nearly hit the 25 KB load limit.
change.instead: Memory is for lasting rules only.

drop.title: "Known reds" that stayed red for weeks
drop.detail: One "base red" was a real bug.

drop.title: History in code comments (ticket numbers, names, dates)
Hand-off files kept after merge, and decisions copied into 4–5 places
The exact test count recorded as if it were the result
drop.detail: Report green or red plus the failures.

drop.title: Five or six records per round (register, ledger, STATUS, review page, status page, ticket)

incidents.what_happened: Two overlapping test runs corrupted 16 settings; recovered from the database log
incidents.rule: Each agent gets its own data, and know the restore path first

incidents.what_happened: An orchestrator's "save everything" swept a builder's live code into a docs commit
incidents.rule: One writer per folder; save files by name; check where you are

incidents.what_happened: "Production down" was the host blocking the office IP, not the plugin
incidents.rule: Find the layer before touching code

incidents.what_happened: Staging looked broken because of a WordPress block's auto-formatting
incidents.rule: Copy production's setup locally; inspect the served page first

incidents.what_happened: The staging page cache showed old data
incidents.rule: Never read state through a cache

incidents.what_happened: CI lints with PHP 7.4 and the laptop had 8.2
A feature passed review; my check with real prices failed it
incidents.rule: Write business rules as a table of real cases first

incidents.what_happened: "Understood" was taken as yes; unreviewed screens got changed
incidents.rule: Confirm the scope in one line

incidents.what_happened: Staging's timezone was wrong, found on launch eve
incidents.rule: Compare environment settings in every release check

incidents.what_happened: Browser tests sent orders to Mailchimp
incidents.rule: Test runs never touch outside services

did_well: Short, clear decisions, recorded word for word.
Checking the real thing on my phone. That caught bugs the tests didn't.
Noticing when the process cost too much and asking for a lighter version "only if we keep the quality".
Keeping sessions narrow ("forget the notes, just fix X").
Adding review where live data is at risk.
Batching feedback per screen instead of drip-feeding it.

principles.title: I own the what and the "done". Claude owns the how, and shows proof.
Proof, not summaries.
principles.detail: "Tests pass" means nothing without the command and its output. A screen change means a screenshot, or I look at it myself.

principles.title: The builder never grades its own work.
principles.detail: Risky changes get a reviewer that did not write them.

principles.title: Small steps.
principles.detail: One change at a time, saved (committed) often, easy to undo.

principles.title: Staging first, always.
principles.detail: Production only after I check it on a real device and say "passed". I do the push to production.

principles.title: Care in proportion to risk.
principles.detail: Words and looks get a quick check. Logic, money, customer data and permissions get the full gate.

principles.title: Lean beats thorough-looking.
principles.detail: Every doc, comment, test and agent costs something. If nobody will read it again, don't write it.

principles.title: One job per session.
principles.detail: A fresh session for each job, started from a short brief.

principles.title: Know the way back before going forward.
principles.detail: Backups, rollback and the "if it breaks" plan exist before launch, not after.

principles.title: I understand the load-bearing parts.
principles.detail: I don't read every line. For the parts that handle money, data and access, I can explain what they do. That is where I learn.

review_gate.rule: A fresh reviewer scores the change 1–10 the way a senior WordPress/WooCommerce developer would. 9 or above passes. Anything below 9 fails. On a fail, fix and re-review. At most 5 review rounds. Still below 9 after round 5 → stop, push the branch, hand it to José with the last report. Never merge on a failing score.

history.event: Cap raised to 5 rounds after #18 needed five (7 → 8 → 8 → 7 → 9)

review_gate.overall_rule: One overall score, not an average; the weakest area drags the overall down.

honesty.label: Schedule
honesty.text: The roadmap target was 2026-08-15; the store went live on 2026-11-01, 78 days later, after the scope grew to include the deli's holiday layer.

honesty.label: Process cost
honesty.text: The project wrote 1.09 million words of docs; STATUS reached 99,000 words and contradicted itself, and 45% of the decision rows were never signed off.

honesty.label: One red
honesty.text: The harness stands at 6,089 assertion lines with one known red (check 18, A349).

honesty.label: No sales data
honesty.text: There is no production order count in the repo, so the site shows no order-volume chart.
